paper_title: The Many Roles for Fluorine in Medicinal Chemistry
mechanistic_insights: Fluorine substitution significantly lowers the pKa of nearby functional groups, such as amines, through strong inductive effects.
Fluorination of aromatic rings is a common strategy to block sites of metabolic oxidation, thereby improving drug stability and pharmacokinetic profiles.
Fluorine atoms can participate directly in protein-ligand binding through interactions like hydrogen bonds or orthogonal dipole interactions with backbone carbonyls.
The introduction of fluorine or trifluoromethyl groups to an aryl ring generally increases lipophilicity, which can be used to enhance properties like CNS penetration.

The development of bench-stable electrophilic (e.g., Selectfluor) and nucleophilic (e.g., DAST) fluorinating reagents has made the selective introduction of fluorine more accessible for medicinal chemists.

quantitative_outcomes.best_performing_conditions: As a review, the paper does not optimize a single reaction but cites many examples. One cited high-yielding reaction is the trifluoromethylation of an a-bromoamide using methyl fluorosulfonyldifluoroacetate (MFSDA) and copper(I) iodide, achieving a 90% yield.
quantitative_outcomes.notes: This is a perspective article reviewing the broad impact of fluorine in medicinal chemistry. It covers effects on physicochemical properties, metabolism, and binding, and gives an overview of various synthetic fluorination methods. It is not a primary research paper focused on cross-coupling optimization.
